node-1.label: Right scrotal swelling rapidly growing over 3 months without local pain

node-2.label: Patient is a 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker, with medical history of hypertension treated with ARB tablet daily and no known allergies

node-3.label: He underwent a puncture at a prior hospital where red-colored fluid was found

node-4.label: No history of trauma or infections including STDs

node-5.label: Physical examination of the scrotum revealed swelling on the right side

why.why: Ultrasound and MRI reveal a multilocular cystic lesion attached to the testis without solid components, contrast enhancement, or testicular abnormality. Pathology shows bland tall columnar cells with no stromal invasion, and IHC is EpCAM/BerEP4 positive, calretinin negative, and ER/PR positive, all favoring a benign mesothelial/epithelial cystic lesion. These expert findings strongly refute a malignant scrotal/testicular neoplasm; serum tumor markers are pending, but the absence of a testicular solid mass makes malignancy very unlikely, so confidence is reduced from 0.62 to 0.08.

Imaging demonstrates a multilocular cystic hematoma attached to the testis with T1-hyperintense contents, consistent with hematocele/hematoma and supporting the bloody aspirate. However, pathology showing bland tall columnar cells with no stromal invasion and an epithelial/mesothelial IHC profile indicates the blood is more likely within a benign cystic lesion rather than a primary traumatic hematoma; the lack of trauma also reduces the likelihood of a simple hematocele. Confidence is modestly increased to 0.3.

The non-inflammatory red aspirate, absence of trauma/STD history, and imaging/pathology showing no inflammatory mass or infectious process all refute scrotal infection/inflammation. The lesion is a multilocular cyst with bland epithelial cells, not an abscess or cellulitis; confidence is reduced to 0.02.

The lesion is a multilocular cystic mass attached to the testis with bloody content and an epithelial lining, not a simple hydrocele. Imaging and pathology indicate a complex benign cystic lesion rather than a simple fluid collection, so benign hydrocele remains very unlikely; confidence is reduced to 0.03.

node-11.label: Pathological examination shows bland tall columnar cells with no stromal invasion in the cyst wall

node-12.label: Immunohistochemistry is positive for EpCAM/BerEP4, negative for calretinin, and positive for ER/PR

node-13.label: MRI shows T1-hyperintense contents within the multilocular cystic lesion

node-14.label: Serum tumor marker results are not yet available

node-15.label: Benign multilocular paratesticular cystic lesion (mesothelial/epithelial origin) with hemorrhage

The bloody aspirate and T1-hyperintense contents are consistent with intralesional hemorrhage. Confidence is 0.85 because serum tumor markers are still pending and definitive confirmation requires surgical excision.
